name: JORDAN

flag.title: Flag of Jordan
flag.note: Black, white & green with red chevron

lead: Jordan is a desert kingdom in the Middle East. A whole city is carved from rose-red rock here. The Dead Sea is so salty that you float without swimming. Bedouin (desert herders) have roamed the sandy land for centuries.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The Great Rift Valley, a huge crack in the ground, splits Jordan's desert. The Dead Sea lies about 430 m below sea level, the lowest place on Earth. Nothing can live in its salty water.
In the south, Wadi Rum (a desert valley) glows orange at sunset.
animals: The Arabian oryx is a white antelope with long straight horns. Hunters wiped it out in the wild. A global rescue programme bred it back, and herds returned to Wadi Rum in 2009.
The sand cat has huge ears, hunts lizards by night, and never needs to drink. Millions of migrating birds visit the Azraq marsh.
culture: Jordanians love welcoming guests. Tiny cups of cardamom coffee keep coming until you tilt yours sideways to say 'enough'.
The national dish, mansaf, is lamb in dried-yoghurt sauce over rice. Friday is the day of rest, with long family lunches after prayers.
history: About 2,000 years ago, the Nabataeans, a desert trading people, carved the city of Petra into rose-red cliffs. They grew wealthy by controlling spice and silk routes.
The Ottomans, from Turkey, ruled for 400 years. Jordan became a kingdom after World War I. King Abdullah II has ruled since 1999. He traces his family back 41 generations to the Prophet Muhammad.
wows: The Dead Sea is about 10 times saltier than the ocean.
In 1812, a Swiss explorer in disguise sneaked into Petra, hidden from outsiders for centuries.
Wadi Rum played Mars in the film 'The Martian'.
Amman, Jordan's capital, is built on seven hills, like Rome.
The Jordan River is barely 30 metres wide because so much water is taken upstream.
Jordan has so little water that, by some counts, only one country has less.
Azraq, a desert marsh, dried up by 1992, but people refilled it and birds returned.

myths.fact: Coffee plants first grew wild in Ethiopia. Traders carried them to Arabia, and later the world.
Snow falls on Amman in some winters. Desert nights can also drop below freezing.
